title: Fitting polystyrene coving with adhesive
subtitle: Measure, mitre, and glue lightweight polystyrene coving at the wall-ceiling junction for a neat decorative finish
excerpt: How to fit polystyrene coving using coving adhesive. Covers marking the cutting line, cutting internal and external mitres with a mitre box, applying adhesive, and filling the joints.
sourceNotes: Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). Reader's Digest Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). UK trade practice for decorating finishes.

glossaryTerms.definition: A ready-mixed or powder adhesive formulated for bonding polystyrene and plaster coving to walls and ceilings. Applied in a thin bead to the back of the coving; sets in 30 to 60 minutes. Also called cornice adhesive.

A 45-degree angled cut on the end of a coving length that allows two pieces to meet neatly at an internal (concave) corner. The two cuts are mirror images and are identified as left-hand and right-hand cuts.

content.text: Polystyrene coving fits at the wall-ceiling junction and gives a room a finished, jointed look. The job is measure, mitre, and glue. You cut the mitres in a simple mitre box, fix the lengths with
, and fill the joints with matching filler. No specialist kit beyond the mitre box.
Mark the cutting lines on the wall and ceiling

Hold a short offcut of coving against the corner and mark a pencil line along the wall face and along the ceiling face. Snap a chalk line or use a long straight edge to continue both lines around the whole room. These lines are the guides for positioning each length when you glue it up. Mark the room perimeter in one pass before mixing any adhesive.

Set the coving in the mitre box with the wall face against the back of the box and the ceiling face against the base. The mitre box has two 45-degree slots: one for left-hand cuts and one for right-hand cuts. An

at an inside corner needs one left-hand and one right-hand cut on the two meeting lengths. Dry-fit the pieces before applying adhesive. Polystyrene cuts cleanly with a fine-tooth tenon saw or a sharp utility knife; keep the blade upright and do not press hard.
Apply the adhesive and fix each length

Apply coving adhesive in a thin, continuous bead along both back faces of the coving (wall face and ceiling face). Press the length firmly into position, aligning the front faces with the pencil lines. Hold for 30 seconds, then let go and move on. The adhesive grabs in a few minutes; support any sagging lengths with temporary panel pins or masking-tape straps until the adhesive sets (about 30 minutes).

Fill any gaps at mitre joints and at the wall and ceiling edges with a flexible decorator's caulk or the coving adhesive itself, squeezed from the tube and smoothed with a wet finger. For square butt joints at the ends of straight runs, fill with a powder filler mixed to a smooth paste. Allow the filler to dry before sanding lightly with 120-grit. The coving can be painted the same day the adhesive has set (check the adhesive tub for the minimum cure time before overpainting).
External corners (convex) use the same mitre box but the cuts are the other way around: right-hand cut meets right-hand cut. Check the mitre box instructions for the slot marked external.
Plaster coving is heavier and needs a stronger adhesive (often a bonding plaster or a specialist coving plaster). The mitre and positioning method is the same but you need to hold each length longer.
On textured ceilings, scrape the textured finish back to bare plaster in the adhesive zone before fixing. Adhesive bonded to textured paint pulls the paint off.

attrs.symptom: Coving pulls away from the ceiling after a few days
attrs.cause: Adhesive applied over a dusty or previously painted surface that was not keyed. The adhesive bonded to the paint, not to the substrate.
attrs.fix: Remove the length, clean off the old adhesive, roughen the back of the coving and the wall/ceiling surface with 80-grit, then re-fix with fresh adhesive.

attrs.symptom: Mitre joint has a visible gap after fixing
attrs.cause: The corner is not a true 90 degrees, or the cuts were not set accurately in the mitre box.
attrs.fix: Fill the gap with flexible decorator's caulk and smooth with a wet finger. For large gaps, cut a new mitre, adjusting the angle slightly.

attrs.symptom: Lengths are not level across the run of the wall
attrs.cause: The pencil lines were marked at different heights at each end of the room because the ceiling is not level.
attrs.fix: Accept the variation or use a spirit level to set the coving at a consistent horizontal line. Polystyrene coving can flex slightly to follow a bowed ceiling.
